- When sentiment is positive (≥0.27) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and forecast is trending up, lower the forecast by 3–5% to account for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast values by 2–4% to correct for momentum decay.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below forecast), adjust next forecast downward by 1–3% to reflect reversion bias.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.27), apply a 2–3% smoothing filter to avoid overfitting to noisy sentiment signals.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.10) over 5+ days, reduce forecast mean by 1–2% to account for subdued market participation.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >3% for 3+ consecutive days, apply a downward correction of 1–2% per day to avoid overestimating upward momentum.
